questions.q: About how old was Kala Nag at the start of the story?
choices: Nearly forty years old
Nearly seventy years old
Just over twenty years old
Close to one hundred years old

questions.q: What advice did Kala Nag's mother, Radha Pyari, give him when he was young?
choices: Always obey the man who sits on your neck
Elephants who are afraid always get hurt
Never trust a tiger, even a wounded one
Save your strength for the hardest work
questions.evidence: elephants who were afraid always got hurt

questions.q: How did Kala Nag learn that his mother's advice was true?
choices: He ran from a tiger and was clawed across the back
He backed in fear into piled rifles and got pricked
He refused to cross a river and was beaten by his driver
He hid from a storm and was left behind by the herd
questions.evidence: the bayonets pricked him in all his softest places

questions.q: What was Kala Nag's special job once the wild elephants were trapped in the stockade?
choices: To beat down the biggest, wildest tusker
To carry the men with ropes into the stockade
To lead the frightened young calves to their mothers
To push the heavy drop gate shut behind the herd
questions.evidence: picking out the biggest and wildest tusker of the mob

questions.q: Kala Nag would go "into that flaring, trumpeting pandemonium." What does "pandemonium" mean?
choices: A deep, muddy pit
Wild, noisy confusion
A quiet forest clearing
A long line of tame animals

questions.q: How did Little Toomai show that the great Kala Nag was "afraid" of him?
choices: He rode him across a deep river all by himself
He called him a fat old pig and made him lift his feet
He took away his food and made him wait for it
He sat on his head and steered him with an ankus
questions.evidence: made him lift up his feet one after the other

questions.q: What kind of life did Big Toomai say he would prefer?
choices: Hunting tigers in the hills with Petersen Sahib
Brick elephant lines, smooth roads and little work
Leading the King's elephant in grand processions
Farming rice by the river with his family

questions.q: Why did Little Toomai say nothing when his father praised the Cawnpore barracks?
choices: He preferred camp life in the hills
He was afraid his father would punish him
He had never been to Cawnpore and could not say
He agreed but did not want to seem lazy
questions.evidence: He very much preferred the camp life

questions.q: What brave thing did Little Toomai do one night during the elephant drive?
choices: He shut the drop gate when the men were too busy
He threw a dropped rope up to a driver in the Keddah
He rode Kala Nag into the stockade without his father
He chased a wild calf back inside with his torch
questions.evidence: threw up the loose end of a rope

questions.q: What happened right after Kala Nag saw Little Toomai down among the elephants?
choices: He picked him up and handed him to Big Toomai
He trumpeted until the men stopped the drive
He stood over the boy to guard him from the wild calf
He carried him out of the stockade to his mother
questions.evidence: caught him in his trunk, and handed him up to Big Toomai

questions.q: Why was Big Toomai so upset that his son had joined in the elephant catching?
choices: He feared Little Toomai would become a hunter, not a mahout
He was jealous that the hunters were paid more than he was
He thought the boy had made Kala Nag disobey him
He had promised Petersen Sahib the boy would stay home
questions.evidence: Petersen Sahib will surely catch thee and make thee a wild hunter

choices: The head of all the Keddah operations
The rich rajah who wanted to buy Kala Nag
The army officer who took Kala Nag to Abyssinia
The clerk who paid the drivers their wages
questions.evidence: He was the head of all the Keddah operations

questions.q: When Petersen Sahib joked that Kala Nag's trick was for stealing green corn, what did Little Toomai answer?
choices: That it was for picking mangoes
That it was for stealing melons
That it was for reaching his bed
That it was for catching birds
questions.evidence: Not green corn, Protector of the Poor,--melons

questions.q: "Except where elephants were concerned, he was just as bashful as a child could be." What does "bashful" mean?
choices: Shy
Rude
Wise
Bold
questions.evidence: he was just as bashful as a child could be

questions.q: What did Petersen Sahib really mean by "Come to me when thou hast seen the elephants dance"?
choices: Come back next year, when you are a little older
Never, since no man has ever seen such a dance
Come back once you have learned to rope a calf
Wait until the big festival in the spring

questions.q: What did the Assamese hill driver say Big Toomai should do that night?
choices: Sleep beside Kala Nag with a burning torch
Double-chain the pickets of all his elephants
Move the new elephants far away from the river
Send the boy back to Petersen Sahib's camp

questions.q: Why did Little Toomai sit before Kala Nag thumping a tom-tom that evening?
choices: To keep the wild elephants away from the camp
To practice for a feast the next morning
He was full of joy that Petersen Sahib had noticed him
His father had told him to call the elephants to supper
questions.evidence: the more he thought of the great honor that had been done to him, the more he thumped

questions.q: What is this part of the story mostly about?
choices: A boy who loves elephant catching and is noticed by its great leader
An old elephant who is sold to a rajah and leads royal processions
A father who teaches his son to become a wild elephant hunter
A group of drivers who race their elephants down to the plains
questions.evidence: Petersen Sahib had noticed him, and given him money
